key_insight: You can postpone the expensive constraint projection until the very end of nonconvex stochastic optimization and still recover an exactly feasible solution with near-optimal stationarity guarantees.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the practical cost of constrained training loops in settings like safe LLM finetuning, transfer learning, and rank-constrained continual learning where projections can dominate runtime.
method: Use a penalized proximal method with only stochastic subgradients during training.
Perform all intermediate updates using simple projections onto a Euclidean ball, not the full constraint set.
Apply one terminal projection to obtain an exactly feasible output; for smooth nonconvex constraints, an exact-penalty variant yields an exactly feasible point near an ε-KKT point.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports oracle-complexity guarantees of \~O(ε^-4) stochastic subgradients with one final projection, and no empirical dataset or benchmark evaluation is described.
watch_item: The guarantee is oracle-complexity only: it does not imply an efficient algorithm exists for projecting onto an arbitrary nonconvex constraint set at the end.
paper_title: Constrained Nonconvex Stochastic Optimization with One Projection
